/answer [auto-answered-by-orchestrator]

Auto-answered by the orchestrator clarify-respond workflow.

DECISIONS:
Q1: A+B
Q2: REFRAME
Q3: REFRAME

RATIONALE:
Q1: In `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, both a matrix job (`orchestrate-poll (1)`) and a local shard inside a job (the `::error::orchestrate-poll shard ${shard} failed (exit N)` line at about line 1644, with 0-based shards from `seq 0`) can carry the name "shard 1". #6886 is closed and its text is not in the checkout. So the target is any `orchestrate-poll` matrix job that failed on PR #6576's recorded head, and within it the local shard 1 section. Taking both readings costs nothing, because the full log of the failed job settles which one it was.
Q2: GITHUB FACTS show that PR #6576 was merged into `main` on 2026-10-09 (head `ai/issue-6573`), so option A's "fix targets that branch" is no longer possible. Reproduction stays tied to the recorded PR head, which is the issue's intent and avoids repeating the earlier main-only attempt that ended BLOCKED. Because that code is now on `main`, any demonstrated fix must target `main`.
Q3: The implement editor has no network or GitHub credential. Option A's "host-side steps" would mean adding new workflow machinery, which is outside this issue's scope. Option B (no PR) and option C alone (no committed artefact) both lead back to the no-op/BLOCKED dead end that stranded #6886. So the reproduction happens in the sandbox with the exact CI partition. The result is either a fix for a reproduced defect or a committed report. The original log is recorded as unavailable from the sandbox rather than treated as a reason to stop.

EXECUTION PLAN (required for any non-letter decision):
Q1:
  strategy: reframe
  inputs:
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml (orchestrate-poll step, ~lines 1585-1650: group split `NR % CI_POLL_TEST_GROUP_COUNT == CI_POLL_TEST_GROUP_INDEX`, shard split `NR % CI_POLL_TEST_SHARDS == shard`, shards numbered from 0)
    - tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py
    - tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py
  steps:
    - Take as the reproduction target group index 1 of 4 (`orchestrate-poll (1)`), local shard 1 of 4 within it. Also run the remaining local shards of that group, so the result covers either reading.
    - If a failing test name becomes available (for example from a later log fetch), it replaces the partition guess.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: "obtain the complete failing shard-1 log" is narrowed to "identify the failing tests by reproducing the exact CI partition" when the log cannot be fetched.
  equivalence_argument: The partition is computed deterministically from the test list in ci.yml, so running the same group and shard selection runs the same tests the failed job ran.
  reversibility: If a human later supplies the real failing job and log, the report is updated or the fix re-targeted. Nothing in CI is changed.
Q2:
  strategy: reframe
  inputs:
    - PR #6576 recorded head (head branch `ai/issue-6573`, merged into `main` 2026-10-09T11:10:46Z)
    - current `main` checkout
  steps:
    - Reproduce against the checked-out tree, which contains #6576's merged content. If a pre-squash head tree is present (for example a preserved `ai/issue-6573` checkout), run the same partition there too and record which tree each run used.
    - Fix a defect only if a test fails reproducibly. The fix goes on the default branch (`main`), because the PR branch is merged and closed.
    - Do not change the aggregate `lint` job, the `needs` list, or the shard and partition logic in ci.yml to make tests pass.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: "fix ... at the PR head" is replaced by "reproduce against #6576's content and fix on `main`, where that content now lives".
  equivalence_argument: A squash merge carries the PR head's tree into `main`, so a defect present at the recorded head is present on `main` unless later commits fixed it. In that case the report records "no longer reproduces".
  reversibility: A fix on `main` is an ordinary PR that can be reverted. No history is rewritten.
Q3:
  strategy: reframe
  inputs:
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml orchestrate-poll step (partition commands)
    - tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py, tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py
    - report path: docs/postmortems/2026-10-10-pr-6576-orchestrate-poll-shard-1.md (follows the existing docs/postmortems/ convention)
  steps:
    - Build the remaining-tests list the way ci.yml does, then select group 1 of 4 and run local shards 0-3 with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py <tests>`. Run the full group 1 partition at most 3 times, and rerun any test that fails once at most 3 times to tell a flake from a deterministic failure.
    - If a test fails reproducibly: fix the demonstrated root cause in the code, or in the test only when documented behaviour shows the test is wrong. Add a regression assertion where it fits, and include a changelog fragment under changelog.d/.
    - If nothing fails: commit only the report. It lists the partition commands, the test count per shard, the pass/fail result of every run, the tree used, and a note that the original job log could not be fetched from the network-isolated sandbox (UNVERIFIED). This is the terminal deliverable and must not be turned into a BLOCKED verdict.
    - Do not add workflow, host-side or log-fetching machinery in this issue.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: "obtain the complete failing shard-1 log, or rerun that check" is replaced by "bounded local reproduction of the exact CI partition, with a committed report when nothing reproduces".
  equivalence_argument: The issue already allows "if bounded reruns pass, report the tests and run results without a speculative code change". A committed report gives the implement run a non-empty diff, so it cannot be classified as a no-op. Required CI still runs on the resulting PR.
  reversibility: The report is one docs file and can be deleted or rewritten if a human later recovers the real log and finds a different cause.
